newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks ease off highs, glitch hits trade.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks ease off highs, glitch hits trade.

text.p: Australian stocks eased off their record highs at Tuesday's opening as traders continued to mark down market heavyweight the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) following its profit warning on Monday.
Trading was also affected by technical problems with the stock exchange's trading system, SEATS.
The All Ordinaries index was 5.3 points lower at 2,579.5 in the first half hour of trade, with the market having little offshore guidance due to market holidays in New York and London.
Brokers said trading was relatively quiet with A$68.7 million (US$52.2 million) worth of market trade.
"It's not going to go a great deal one way or the other," said Peter Struk a dealer at Reynolds & Co.
"BHP will have to come off a bit further yet because of the downgrading, so you will probably see a bit of buying coming into Western's (WMC) and MIM's," Struk said.
Analysts have downgraded their earnings forecasts for BHP following Monday's announcement that it expected a flat performance until it restructured and started new projects.
BHP was 16 cents down at A$18.76 in morning trade.

The fall added to the A$760 million wiped off BHP's market value on Monday, when it fell 40 cents. "With both the big overseas markets closed, we obviously lack in general direction and I expect a pretty quiet day with low volumes and narrow ranges," said Steve Mayne, a dealer at Brisbane broker Nevitts.

Banking and insurance shares paused for breath after strong gains following Friday's surprise cut in cash rates by the Reserve Bank. Shares of retailers and building related companies were also steady after receiving a boost from the interest rate cut.
